簡易説明: The morning information program 'Oha-Oha! Japan'
詳細説明 cha 1688: The morning information program of Japonica TV, Japan's largest private television station. 'Lightning Thunder-Visit♪ Yukipin', broadcast from 6:50, is its high-rated main segment, in which Japonica TV's popular female announcer, Ms. Yukino Shinbashi, visits famous spots all over Japan every day. It is no exaggeration to say that this rating is kept up by the popularity of announcer Yukino Shinbashi, and Japonica TV is apparently desperate to stay one step ahead so that she does not become a freelance announcer. [TN: "thunder-visit" puns on the Japanese word for "visit".]\n　Comments posted on the popular social network 'Shabetter' can be shown within the program, but on very rare occasions the censoring function fails, the posted comment goes out in the program exactly as posted, and it causes an on-air accident; this too is a hidden charm of the program.

簡易説明: The movie 'Fascination'
詳細説明 cha 1688: A movie released in the summer of Shiyo 799. It was originally a late-night moe anime, a story that begins with the heroine, the high school girl 'Makoto Amachi', selling her soul to another demon to save a friend attacked by a demon. While leading an ordinary student life, Makoto drives off the demonic threats that fall on her friends using the demon's power 'D Energy', but through the side effects of the overused 'D Energy' Makoto becomes enthralled by the demon, and in the end even tries to take her friends' lives; that is how it develops.\n　This anime won enormous support from some enthusiasts, and when it was later exported overseas its popularity heated up further, until at last even a Hollywood live-action movie was made. This DVD is that reimported version, and among fans of the original there is a tendency to mock female fans who do not know the original as 'reverse-moe women'.\n　Incidentally, Makoto's catchphrase is "Be reborn as a pure demon! Devil Justice!"

簡易説明: Social network site　Shabetter
詳細説明 cha 1688: A social network site made by an Australian student to study Japanese. Before anyone knew it, it spread to students of Japanese all over the world as ideal for studying Japanese.\n　Now its usage rate among Japanese people is also high, and interests seem to coincide on the points 'information from around the world comes in in Japanese, which is very convenient' and 'you can easily make friends with foreigners'.\n　However, its user population worldwide is just under 100 million, so seen globally, Shabetter is a very niche social network site.

簡易説明: A cherry variety commonly seen in Japan　Somei-yoshino
詳細説明 cha 1688: A Japanese-born variety produced by crossing an Edo-higan-line cherry with an Oshima-zakura-line cherry, and the representative species of present-day ornamental cherries. Genetic research has found that it is a clone originating from a single tree, and all the trees in every region were propagated by human hands through grafting and the like. Seeds with purely Somei-yoshino parents never germinate, and pure offspring from natural crossing between Somei-yoshino trees are impossible.

簡易説明: French tea  Pierre Palais
詳細説明 cha 1688: A company founded about 300 years ago by French tea lovers; the company name is also the brand name of the product. Few of France's colonies at the time had land that grew tea, and the country soon moved to a coffee culture, so tea is said to have been a rather minor drink. Just because of that, those who loved tea then seem to have held a policy of their own, and it is said to have been handed down unbroken to the present day.\n　Pierre Palais is now imported from contract tea farms in Sri Lanka, and is marked by a strong yet fruity aroma. Its sweetness is stronger than its bitterness, so it is held to be better enjoyed straight than as milk tea or lemon tea. That strong flavor also means it can be chilled over ice and still give the full taste of tea.

簡易説明: Shiyo, the era name used in this work
詳細説明 cha 1688:
This work uses one fixed era name throughout. Its "Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse]" corresponds to the year Shiyo 800.
　Of the characters, Natsumi Kogori was born in Shiyo 783, Haruka Niimura in 782 and Erina Goto in Shiyo 784. Akane Kogori, Natsumi Kogori's mother, and Mifuyu Niimura, Haruka Niimura's mother, were both born in Shiyo 757.
　In Shiyo 1 an event greatly changed where authority lay in Japan, and the era name has been used ever since. In the present day of Shiyo 800 that change of authority is not much thought about; the constitution grants the "three great rights of the people", the right to life, the right to education and the right to take part in government, and sets the three great duties of education, labor and taxation. The separation of powers holds, with the cabinet as the executive, the Diet as the legislature and the courts as the judiciary, and the Mikado stands as the symbol of Japan. This imperial line existed before the Shiyo era began, however, and the common reading is that the country of Japan has continued for more than 2000 years. The year before Shiyo 1, for example, is called Pre-Shiyo 1.
　In short, the Shiyo 800 of this world differs little from the Japan of the real world, but only in the present day: its historical events are greatly different.

物名: スペシャルステーキランチ
簡易説明: Zahha lunch menu  Special Steak Lunch
詳細説明 cha 1688: A lunch menu item that appeared out of nowhere in Shiyo 800. It lavishes a full pound of meat, about 450 grams, on the plate, a power lunch with real substance. Rice and miso soup or bread and soup can be chosen. Even so, the price is an abnormally cheap 680 yen including tax. Zahha is low-priced across the board to begin with, but even so this is no ordinary price.\n　Because of that, the rumors never stop: that it is not beef, that it must be something else made to look like meat. In fact the health center and the consumer center did once look into the abnormal price, and it appears to be genuine beef. Asked how it can be served at such a price, the president would say only that it was the result of company effort.\n　Since the item carries that sort of history, fans whisper that one day it will suddenly be dropped from the menu, and they keep going back to Zahha to enjoy the Special Steak Lunch while they can. That is in fact Zahha's aim: serving beef worth 100 yen a gram at cost, and using a dish that draws rumors like these to build up fans of Zahha itself and bring the customers in. Company effort indeed.

物名: 古郡なつみの予知能力
簡易説明: Natsumi Kogori's ability to foresee danger
詳細説明 cha 1688:
Natsumi Kogori is said to have an ability to sense danger. It comes with conditions, however:
・the cherry trees are in bloom
・she sees the person who will meet the danger
・or she hears the voice of the person who will meet the danger
・limited to a future between about 10 seconds and 10 days away
such are the conditions. In other words, by being near Natsumi Kogori in cherry blossom season you can learn of a danger in the near future and plan around it. Even Erina Goto, who believes in no supernatural phenomenon and no ghost, is convinced that Natsumi Kogori's foresight of danger is an ability that cannot be doubted, so although the mechanism is unknown its reliability appears to be very high. It works on danger to Natsumi Kogori herself as well.
　It seems, however, that foreseeing danger needs something beyond the conditions above, and what that element is remains unknown.

簡易説明: The year-end special program 'Psycho Land'
詳細説明 cha 1688: A special television program compiling paranormal phenomena, broadcast every year on New Year's Eve. It is broadcast from 18:00 in the evening until 0:30 the next day (the new year), and viewers greet the new year before they know it while watching paranormal phenomena. They range from gossipy ones to serious ones, and every year it takes up several paranormal phenomena and explains them. Being this kind of program, as expected, it has quite exaggerated staging, but such programs have become markedly fewer in recent years, so, on the contrary, some say a program like this is fresh. It seems popular especially among elementary and junior high school students, and on New Year's Eve, how to seize the right to choose the channel from their parents is their last task of the year.\n　Its ratings are not very strong, but its sponsors range from major occult magazine publishers to travel agencies planning mystery tours abroad, and for people who watch this program, the commercials themselves are said to be very interesting too.

簡易説明: A local paper published in Motoki-cho, Sawa Prefecture　The Motoki Daily
詳細説明 cha 1688: The Motoki Daily is, literally, a local paper distributed within Motoki-cho. It boasts a tremendous subscription rate of about 70 percent of Motoki-cho households, and its selling point is fair and detailed information. However, not that many big events happen in Motoki-cho itself every day, and its main content is, if anything, reporting from visits to public institutions and companies; articles on incidents or politics are hardly seen.\n　The reason such a local paper has this many subscribers is that it comes with coupons usable in the town every day. A coupon can be used by reading the QR code printed in the paper with a cell phone or the like and showing it at the store. These coupons have a good reputation, and companies compete to get their QR codes into the paper. By the way, to win the right to place a QR code, besides the listing fee there is a lottery, so luck is needed too.\n　For subscribers as well, which places' coupons will be in the paper that day is said to be a daily pleasure.

簡易説明: Video-sharing site　MOVLIFE
詳細説明 cha 1688: Users who have registered an account can upload video data freely and at no charge and make it public to an unspecified number of people. It has fewer users than the largest video streaming service, but its uploaders seem to tend to take on all kinds of challenges and post those chaotic videos, and it boasts enormous popularity among users who like such videos.\n　Popular right now is an American uploader called Crazy cowboy, who takes on reckless challenges every time and comes to grief. He apparently has connections in the police and the military, and even for challenges that would normally never get permission from the police and others, he gets their cooperation, which is also a factor boosting his popularity.

簡易説明: A fierce carbonated drink  Ultra Fizz Bomber
詳細説明 cha 1688:
A carbonated drink put on sale in Shiyo 799 by the Japanese food maker Catastrophic Foods. It uses no sugar and is marked by a faint citrus scent. Its greatest feature is its fierce carbonation: it holds dozens of times the carbon dioxide of an ordinary fizzy drink. Because of that, against 500ml of content the bottle can alone weighs a full kilogram.
　The gas is dissolved in by a special technique, and in the mouth it strikes the mucous membrane like a firecracker, so most people who drink it for the first time spit it straight out on the spot. Some become addicted to that sting, however, and their fervor is mocked as close to religious.
　Special technique or not, shaking it lets the carbonation out all at once, and accidents in which the bottle fires off like an arrow on opening never stop. For this reason a bill to amend the law with an upper limit on carbon dioxide in fizzy drinks is due to go before the Diet shortly.
　The color of a pressure marker sticker on the bottom of the bottle tells you whether it will erupt, so that such accidents do not happen, but many even among the fervent fans do not know it.

簡易説明: Motoki new money who made their fortune in Motoki-cho real estate
詳細説明 cha 1688: As Motoki-cho's population has grown, land prices have soared since around Shiyo 790, and real estate dealers and individual investors who took notice are all buying up property; such people are called the Motoki new money. Moreover, because wealthy people able to buy such property are flowing into Motoki-cho, the wealthy newcomers and the middle-class-and-below residents who have lived in Motoki-cho all along often do not get along. However, there are also landowners who held vast tracts in Motoki-cho from the start, and as they sell their land, a second generation of Motoki new money is appearing one after another.\n　Children raised in Motoki new money families almost never go on to the high school in Motoki-cho, so it is said there has so far been no case of this developing into bullying or problem behavior. They do not go to the high school in Motoki-cho 'because its deviation score is low,' and go on instead to high schools in Minakami City, the prefectural capital.

簡易説明: The bug Daijiro Ise left at the Goto home
詳細説明 cha 1688: A battery-type bug weighing about 40 grams. Its effective range is thought to be a few dozen meters. Details unknown.

簡易説明: Ephedrine
詳細説明 cha 1688: Ephedrine is a sympathomimetic used as a decongestant or to treat low blood pressure during local anesthesia, an alkaloid derived from ephedra, a gymnosperm used as a crude drug in kampo medicine. Because it has the effect of stimulating the sympathetic nerves, it is designated a doping drug, and its use at the Olympics and sports competitions is prohibited. It is contained as an active ingredient in kakkonto and asthma medicines, and in proper amounts it does not harm health. However, ephedrine is a precursor of methamphetamine, a stimulant drug, and abuse is against the law, so care is needed.\n　Also, there is a popular belief that cherry pollen contains ephedrine, but at present no scientific evidence exists to prove it.

物名: アポカリプティックサウンド
簡易説明: A strange-sound phenomenon of unknown cause　The Apocalyptic Sound
詳細説明 cha 1688: Since the Shiyo 780s, sounds of scraping metal and sounds like brass instruments have been observed all over the world, and they are called the apocalyptic sound. Searching the internet for this word brings up many videos; people all over the world are aware of its existence, and it is made much of as an occult phenomenon, a sound announcing the end.

簡易説明: The king of hell　Abaddon
詳細説明 cha 1688: In Hebrew it means "place of destruction", "one who destroys" and "the bottom of the abyss", and it is also called the king of locusts and the king of the abyss (hell). In Japanese it is also written "Abadon".　It is depicted as a being that, together with four divine messengers, keeps inflicting on humans a torment lasting several months. The apocalyptic sound is said to be sounded by these divine messengers, and it is also said that this announces, in other words, the end of the world.

物名: 元木桜祭りの大食い大会
簡易説明: The eating contest of the Motoki Cherry Blossom Festival
詳細説明 cha 1688: An eating contest held every year at the Motoki-cho cherry-blossom festival. It began in Shiyo 798, and Erina Goto has won it two years running by an overwhelming margin. Erina Goto, shy by nature, entered such a conspicuous contest because Natsumi Kogori encouraged her to try. From around then, Erina Goto apparently became able to carry herself with confidence even in front of others, so the contest is also the event that brought her cheerful personality to the surface.\n　Even the organizers are vague about the event's name, and it is called the 'Motoki Eating Contest,' the 'Cherry Blossom Festival Eating Festival' and so on. The challenge dishes are mainly things sold at the festival stalls: frankfurters in Shiyo 798, takoyaki in Shiyo 799 and sauce yakisoba in Shiyo 800. Erina Goto's records were 31 frankfurters and 150 takoyaki in 15 minutes, but she is apparently sensitive to hot food and bad at eating it quickly; by her own account, had it not been hot she could have kept going.
表示名: Motoki Cherry Blossom Festival Eating Contest

簡易説明: The children's occult book 'The World of Curses'
詳細説明 cha 1688: An occult learning book for children published by Kobosha. 700 yen before tax. It was originally planned as a study book for schoolchildren, but Kobosha also puts out the long-running occult magazine 'M', and its content was apparently rewritten bit by bit into something more serious.\n　Its content mainly covers curses and magic, presenting occult stories that really exist around the world in a way children can understand. However, it has been rearranged in all sorts of ways: it mixes paper dolls with African sorcery, as in the main story, and for something as famous in Japan as Kokkuri-san it uses a photo of the face of the person you want to curse instead of a 10-yen coin, so it is rather careless. Behind these rearrangements was the question of how many curses could be packed into the page count of a children's book, which made it necessary to force various curse methods together.\n　However, since it contains expressions a little too extreme for a children's book kept at a school, it was rarely actually stocked at schools, and the usual way to get it was from a library or by online shopping (this is why Haruka Niimura could not find the book at school).

簡易説明: Zahha's original menu item 'Russian-Roulette Takoyaki'
詳細説明 cha 1688: Russian-roulette takoyaki, an event menu item at Zahha. It has existed since the restaurant opened in Shiyo 790, but because it was so extreme it was shelved for a time. Fervent requests from some fans brought it back in Shiyo 799. You can order any number of pieces and also choose how many are duds. A dud contains one of habanero, wasabi, Japanese mustard or Black Death Devil Pepper, and each takoyaki is colored to suggest a spice. But red does not necessarily mean habanero, nor yellow Japanese mustard, so first-time players are baffled by the rules. Another feature is the pointlessly elaborate staging: the takoyaki come in a container shaped like a coffin, and smoke billows out when you open the lid. As takoyaki, though, the quality is very high, and players lucky enough to avoid a dud savor the distinctive flavors. With no duds, you can simply enjoy these unusual takoyaki, so it has many child fans too.

物名: ブラック・デス・デビル・ペッパー
簡易説明: The world's strongest spice 'Black Death Devil Pepper'
詳細説明 cha 1688: An artificial spice invented by the seasoning maker 'Simon Spice,' headquartered in America, abbreviated BDDP. Its Scoville rating (a unit of spiciness) is 16 million, equal to 100% pure crystals of capsaicin, the pungent compound in chili peppers (Tabasco is 1,200 Scoville). Naturally, eating it would normally kill you, so it is not for sale. Zahha, however, set its sights on BDDP and succeeded in negotiating with Simon Spice to sell it to them specially. Because it is a spice that normally cannot be eaten, a thick contract governs how it is handled. The amount served to customers is especially strict: no more than one part in 100,000 of the whole dish. So for a 20-gram takoyaki, it is a tiny 2 milligrams (about 20 grains of salt). Even so, its effect on the body is tremendous, bringing sweating, tears, hyperventilation and a drop in blood pressure, and you cannot even stand for a while. Naturally, the president of Zahha knows its taste well, and apparently ate no fewer than 200 BDDP takoyaki before it became a product.

簡易説明: What funerals in the Arata settlement are like
詳細説明 cha 1688: In the Arata settlement there is an unusual custom: at a funeral, every mourner wears a Noh mask and red robes. Furthermore, the dead are called 'shinigami,' and the deceased too are dressed in a Noh mask and red robes. The Arata settlement also places great weight on ceremonial occasions; there is no precedent for the common practice of 'moving the date to a weekend,' and everyone in the settlement is obliged to attend every memorial service up to the twelfth-anniversary memorial service.\n　Therefore, Mifuyu Niimura missing a funeral 'for work reasons,' as in the Jusatsu Arc [Killing by Curse] and the Meicho Arc [Clear Sign], is in principle not permitted. It is not allowed without very serious reasons, and in Mifuyu Niimura's case, missing her own husband's funeral is unthinkable. Not only in the Arata settlement: even in society at large, being the only one not to attend a parent's, child's or spouse's funeral is often seen as lacking common sense, so it is thought that Mifuyu Niimura missed it for a grave and urgent reason.\n　Haruka Niimura, however, is missing this twelfth-anniversary memorial service. Her reason is that 'if I attend, something like the Megasawa City case might happen,' and Mifuyu Niimura has reportedly already informed the settlement (whether she gave the reason as it is, is unknown). If she really did inform them, it is unclear whether absence is allowed for such a reason; if she did not, she may have informed them on the day of the service of circumstances, such as illness, that kept Haruka Niimura from coming.

簡易説明: The bug planted in Haruka Niimura's smartphone
詳細説明 cha 1688: For Haruka Niimura's safety, Mifuyu Niimura asked Ryoji Kogori to plant a bug in her smartphone. She chose a bug over an app, which is comparatively easy to plant, because she feared security tools and the like would reveal the app, but Ryoji Kogori lacked the skill to write an app himself or to have a bug send audio data in real time. So he installed one of the bugging apps found anywhere, and, to make it look as if there were a bug, used an old battery and an insulating alloy weighing about 10 grams. At a glance, this made it look as if a bug were drawing on the battery and the smartphone were heavier by that much. This was also meant to fool Mifuyu Niimura's eyes, but he was counting on the slim chance that Haruka Niimura would eventually notice the battery running down fast, consult Erina Goto, and that Erina Goto would find her way to the bug. To Ryoji Kogori it did not matter whether the bugging app was discovered; all he needed was to make Haruka Niimura distrust Mifuyu Niimura. In the Meicho Arc, just as Ryoji Kogori planned, Erina Goto managed to find the bug, which led to Mifuyu Niimura's arrest.

簡易説明: 'Mountain Seclusion', the rite of passage for marrying into the Arata settlement
詳細説明 cha 1688: A woman who wishes to marry a man of the Arata settlement must shut herself away alone for one year on Mount Itohime, at the edge of the Arata settlement, and is forced to live a life of survival. The Arata settlement has a tradition that women too must be strong, and this is how they are trained in body and mind. Very few women can endure such a trial, and it also tests the will: whether she is resolved to marry a man of Arata even if it means enduring this trial. Basically, before going into the mountain she is taught how to make fire, how to hunt animals, how to tell which plants are edible, how to handle weapons and so on, but she may not bring firearms and can use only blades and blunt weapons. And until she comes down the mountain on her own, no one comes to check on her.\n　This mountain seclusion must be completed not only by those who wish to marry in but also by every woman born in the settlement as she comes of age. For this reason the women of the Arata settlement are rich in survival knowledge and acquire physical abilities that do not fall short of the men's (in muscular strength they cannot match men, but they excel instead in reflexes, dynamic vision and agility). There are, however, cases in which the mountain seclusion is waived; they apply to women judged to already have the corresponding physical ability and knowledge before coming of age.\n　Note that only while undergoing the mountain seclusion is one not permitted to take part in weddings and funerals, the important events of the Arata settlement.

物名: 荒田集落から送られた道具
簡易説明: The weapons Mifuyu Niimura ordered from the Arata settlement
詳細説明 cha 1688: To kill two children without leaving evidence, Mifuyu Niimura ordered from the Arata settlement a Noh mask, red robes, a knife, a nata, a mace, and a drug that boosts physical ability. Detailed instructions also seem to have come with them so that the drug could be used safely. Apart from these, Mifuyu Niimura did on-site research in order to carry out the killings, and prepared instructions noting the targets' patterns of movement, the places to carry out the killings, and so on.
表示名: Tools Sent from the Arata Settlement

簡易説明: Parkour
詳細説明 cha 1688: Parkour is a method of drawing out and pursuing the physical ability people inherently have, using movement, and today it is practiced as a sport that originated in France. Making use of walls and terrain and practicing movements such as running, jumping and climbing in combination, one trains every ability needed for daily life and sports. Because there are no rules governing the movements, it is practiced not as a competition but as voluntary exercise. To practice parkour, one must train body and mind every day, cultivate a sense for judging distance and danger, and have the ability to adapt to any situation. For that reason, imitating the kind of moves that appear in online videos soon after starting parkour is dangerous behavior that carries the possibility of death. Therefore it is important for beginners to condition their bodies through training.\n　A similar sport is freerunning, but whereas freerunning is a sport that emphasizes performance, parkour emphasizes moving quickly and efficiently.

簡易説明: Land owned by the state
詳細説明 cha 1688:
The Arata district, which includes the Arata settlement, is designated state-owned land.
・All tenant land of absentee landlords
・Of resident landlords' tenant land, all tenant land beyond 4 chobu in Hokkaido and 1 chobu in the other prefectures
・Tenant land and the like where total holdings exceeded 12 chobu in Hokkaido or 3 chobu in the other prefectures
were sold to the tenant farmers who had actually been working them.
　The aim was to free land that had been ruled by the powerful for centuries under the old feudal system; the state bought it cheaply and sold it off. Paddies and farmland were freed actively in this way, but the process was not thorough for forests and fields, so some land still remains state-owned.
　The Arata district is said to be one of these, never having been a target for sale. However, the people who originally lived in the Arata district were not the powerful, so it is unnatural that the state bought it up. For this reason much is unclear today about why the Arata district became state-owned land. Also, a revision of the Agricultural Land Act abolished the system of buying and selling farmland to create owner-farmers. So there is no longer any point in the state holding state-owned farmland and its early disposal is called for, but the Arata district alone does not fall under this.
　One theory holds that, because the Arata district has many rare animals and plants, it was designated state-owned land to protect them. Perhaps for that reason, food produced in the Arata settlement is rarely seen in the outside world.

簡易説明: Yomotsuhegui
詳細説明 cha 1688: Yomotsuhegui is the idea in Japanese mythology of eating the food of the afterlife, or food made with the utensils of the afterlife. By this a person can live on in the world of Yomi, but in exchange is no longer accepted by the world of the living and simply wanders another world. There are various interpretations of yomotsuhegui: the common one, as above, is that it decides whether one is accepted into a particular world, but another theory says the food of Yomi is so enticing that one cannot return to the world of the living, and even if one does return, food will no longer go down one's throat and one starves to death. By extension, it can also be used to mock people who grow so used to foreign food and life that they look down on their own country, so-called 'Western wannabes.'

簡易説明: The rite of succeeding as a witch
詳細説明 cha 1688:
The Arata settlement has a post called witch, which customarily oversees the settlement's ceremonies. The conditions for becoming a witch are:
・being a woman
・being an adult
・having a dead mother
・being of the Niimura family
and the rite consists of breaking the gravestone, releasing the soul of the buried mother, and receiving that soul. For it, Noh masks and red robes are worn, and the Grand Witch attends the rite. On the way from the house to the graveyard they meet no one, and neither the new witch nor the Grand Witch ever sees the other's bare face. Mifuyu Niimura has also gone through the succession rite, so it seems that being from the Arata settlement, and the mother truly being buried in the graveyard, are not necessarily conditions for becoming a witch.

簡易説明: The occult magazine 'M', which collects paranormal phenomena
詳細説明 cha 1688: An occult magazine launched in Shiyo 745 by the publisher 'Kobosha', which has held occult fans captive for more than half a century since. Its content feels occult through and through: even things that a little thought would show could be proven scientifically, it concludes one by one are the work of paranormal phenomena, UMA or UFOs. In the late 20th century especially, spirit photos and sighting photos of UFOs and UMA were tremendously popular, to the point that reading this magazine had become a status symbol among elementary school students.\n　Being a magazine with this kind of concept, it writes that incidents that actually happened and made the news were paranormal phenomena or unknown phantoms, yet once the incident is solved, the topic quietly vanishes from the next month's issue on.

簡易説明: 'Witch,' a post in the Arata settlement
詳細説明 cha 1688: The Arata settlement has a post called 'witch.' It is something like a priest, and an adult woman who has lost her mother can take it up after going through the succession rite. There are several witches in the settlement, and the one chosen among them as head becomes the Grand Witch, serving as officiant and as the settlement's representative. Erika Niimura is the Grand Witch, Mifuyu Niimura has also become a witch, and Chigaya Niimura, who turned 20 as of April Shiyo 800, is to inherit the name of witch on the day before the memorial service. 'Succession' means taking over the role of witch from the mother of the woman newly appointed; in this case, from Chigaya Niimura's mother.\n　Only women can inherit the name of witch, which suggests that in the Arata settlement women hold more power than men.
表示名: The Witches of the Arata Settlement

簡易説明: A register recording the birth and death dates of the Arata settlement residents
詳細説明 cha 1688: In the Arata settlement, when a child is born, or when someone comes to put down roots in the settlement, their name and date of birth are entered in this register, and when they die, the date and cause of death are entered. This is the Arata version of a family register, and from it one can learn roughly when most residents were born and died.\n　Note that the Arata settlement is state-owned land and belongs to no municipality, so its residents have no official family register, and this register serves as a de facto one. (When an official family register is needed, the Iizawa Prefectural Office can issue one as a special case.)

簡易説明: Kishotenketsu in logical thinking
詳細説明 cha 1688: In films and novels, the 'setup' of kishotenketsu is often stated outright. Through inversion the setup may appear in the latter half, but once the setup is clear, it leads on to the development, twist and conclusion. In logical thinking about real problems, however, one must find the setup oneself. By the time one thinks of it, one is usually already at the development or the twist, so one must consider 'why did the present situation come about?' If one's grasp of this setup is off, one will misjudge even the present that stems from it, and end up at an unwanted conclusion. In other words, accurately finding 'what the cause is' leads to the desired result.

簡易説明: Erina Goto's analysis of the old people's suicides
詳細説明 cha 1688: Kikyo Niimura, the Grand Witch three generations back, is the only one in the last 100 years who did not die in April. After she died, her family was killed and their names were erased from the residents' register. Erina Goto's analysis: 'Dying in April became proof of being an Arata resident; Kikyo Niimura was seen as an outsider threatening the settlement, and her family was killed. Because of this, the old people came to think their families might be killed if they did not die in April, and to protect their families they killed themselves at 75, an age when they could die at any time.'\n　Yet if that were so, Erika Niimura shows no sign of thinking 'I will kill myself when I turn 75,' and it must be called baffling that every old person, without exception, killed themselves without the survivors of Shiyo 800 learning why.

簡易説明: Erina Goto's view of kishotenketsu
詳細説明 cha 1688: According to Erina Goto, thinking about a case like this one in terms of kishotenketsu is very dangerous. Normally, in a work of fiction, the 'setup' is given, and the rule is to start thinking from there. But from the culprit's standpoint, the 'setup,' the occurrence of the case, exists only because there is first a goal, the 'conclusion.' Also, kishotenketsu gives a story its ups and downs, and the culprit's ideal is for the case to be complete with only the 'setup' and the 'conclusion.'

簡易説明: The only cherry tree left in the Arata settlement
詳細説明 cha 1688: As of Shiyo 800, there is only one cherry tree in the Arata district, the Arata settlement included. The other cherry trees were all taken away by some group about 70 years ago.
表示名: The Cherry Tree of the Arata Settlement

物名: 新村幸太郎の殺人教唆
簡易説明: Kotaro Niimura's incitement of his daughters to murder
詳細説明 cha 1688: Chigaya Niimura claims that Kotaro Niimura made her train to kill. Her reason is that he told them to hunt with a nata and a mace, which is weak grounds for calling it incitement to murder. But thanks to it, the sisters have high physical ability, and they could likely kill a person swiftly without even using firearms. Chigaya Niimura may have reasons, with a nuance only she understands, for thinking she was made to train to kill, but at present they are unknown.\n　At the very least, though, it is probably a fact that Kotaro Niimura meant to give his daughters high physical ability. He is also said to have constantly told his daughters to "grow strong to take revenge on the one who killed your mother," and if that came from a pure desire for revenge, it makes some sense as a way of giving his daughters the fighting ability to make revenge possible. However, Chigaya Niimura thinking of it as "training to kill" is a clear contradiction, because by her logic "the daughters would have to kill their father." In other words, if Kotaro Niimura is the culprit, it can only mean that he wants to be killed by his daughters.

簡易説明: The three buggies of the Arata settlement
詳細説明 cha 1688: The Arata settlement has three buggies. They are suited to getting around the mountains of the Arata district smoothly, and the cars the settlement used to have were sold in their place. The road from Arata Station to the settlement was always very rough, and in rainy weather even four-wheel drives often got stuck. Since the buggies were brought in, the range they can cover has grown, and the abandoned hut (rest stop) that was used before is no longer used.

簡易説明: Intuitions other than the ability to foresee danger
詳細説明 cha 1688: Natsumi Kogori can usually foresee danger by meeting, or hearing the voice of, a person who will meet danger, but in exceptional cases she seems to see past events, and moreover events involving people she has not met and whose voices she has not heard. Also, while she usually foresees danger by hearing, in Eiichiro Niimura's voice, she sometimes sees it visually. On the Shigatsu Arc route she has so far recognized danger as Eiichiro Niimura's voice almost without exception, but on other routes there were cases that did not fit.

簡易説明: Droga, a drug made from the roots of the Arata cherry
詳細説明 cha 1688: Droga is a loanword meaning 'drug' in Portuguese. In the Arata settlement, the drug was made by harvesting cherry roots and refining them. Its effect is very great: it can remove the limiter on muscle strength that normally works to protect the body. In other words, it can deliberately trigger the superhuman strength people show in an emergency. Humans are said to normally use only 20 to 30 percent of their full strength; if they used 100%, their bones and muscles would be destroyed. Being such a dangerous drug, misusing it would surely ruin a person.

簡易説明: About the memorial services held in the Arata settlement
詳細説明 cha 1688: Unlike ordinary ones, memorial services in the Arata settlement have every mourner wear a Noh mask and red robes. When the ceremony begins, each person stabs two knives into the Noh mask and red robes laid on a stand. Once that is done, a liquid called falsificaso is dripped into boiling giant bullfrog oil, and finally the Grand Witch cuts apart the red robes on the stand and smashes the Noh mask. It thus takes a form unthinkable at an ordinary funeral, and throughout, the mourners exchange not a single word.
表示名: Memorial Services of the Arata Settlement

簡易説明: Beta-endorphin, a neurotransmitter
詳細説明 cha 1688: A type of neurotransmitter that works in the brain. Because it brings pain relief, an elevated mood and a sense of happiness, it is also called the brain's own narcotic. It is known to be released during sex, when eating delicious food, or during sustained intense exercise, and to have 80 times the painkilling effect of morphine, the famous analgesic. Using Droga appears to bring pain relief through beta-endorphin; besides the superhuman strength people show in an emergency, it brings a sense of elation and puts the body in a condition better suited to fighting.

簡易説明: How often fathers bathe with their middle or high school daughters
詳細説明 cha 1688: Just how common is it for a father and his daughter, particularly one in middle or high school, to bathe together? To answer this question on all your minds, the creative circle New++ conducted its own investigation (strictly for the purpose of raising the quality of this work). In the course of it, we found an article on 'Shirabee,' a news site that surveys topics the public is curious about in ranking form, so we report it here. The respondents were 333 women in their 20s and 30s. The share who bathed with their father until they entered middle school was a little over 10%, and the share who did so until they entered high school was 5 to 10%. In other words, if a class has 15 high school girls, 1 or 2 of them were bathing with their father. Asked why they bathed together, some gave efficiency-based reasons, such as "There was a TV show I wanted to watch, and when I wanted to get in the bath before it started, it didn't matter who was in there," "Our times just happened to overlap, no particular reason," and "We were a big family, and everyone after us was waiting," while other respondents cited closeness, such as "I liked talking in the bath," "We got along well," and "No reason, it was just a normal everyday thing." As this shows, a teenage girl bathing with her father is not extremely rare, and one has to say it is tactless to declare it "impossible" or call her "a daddy's girl."\n\nSource: https://sirabee.com/2015/06/05/34214/

簡易説明: The Grand Witch's Noh mask that Erika Niimura entrusted to Natsumi Kogori
詳細説明 cha 1688: A metal Noh mask passed down through the generations of Grand Witches. For all its strength and sturdiness it is light, and it is made so that it does not tire the wearer even when worn for a long time. It was entrusted to Natsumi Kogori as a kind of amulet when she escaped the Arata settlement, and because she had it tucked inside her clothes, she escaped fatal injury even from Kotaro Niimura's attack. At Erika Niimura's funeral, it was returned to its owner.

簡易説明: The Arata settlement's children's song 'The Princess Song'
詳細説明 cha 1688:
A children's song of unknown authorship. It has been handed down in the Arata settlement since long ago, and the children have grown familiar with this song. The residents' view is that some event was made into a children's song, but no writings about the Princess Song exist, and the lyrics too have all been handed down orally.
　The accepted view is that it already existed by Shiyo 100, and it is thought to be a song made within 100 years of the founding of the Arata settlement. However, because it has been handed down orally, it is unknown whether its content has stayed unchanged since it was made, but since most of the lyrics are words still understood today, it is thought to have been changed as needed into lyrics easy for children to understand.

簡易説明: Falsificaso
詳細説明 cha 1688: A colorless, transparent liquid whose name means 'fake' in Portuguese. It appears as a by-product when Droga is produced, and as of Shiyo 800 it is used in place of incense at funerals. But when heated strongly it gives off a terrible stench, and smelling it directly makes people ill. In fact, falsificaso is a wonder drug that corrects the murderous intent caused by the green eyes; injecting it has been confirmed to eliminate the murderous intent and cure the green eyes. Why such a substance forms when Droga is produced is unknown, but since it is made at least from components originally contained in the roots of the Arata cherry, some causal link is assumed.

シナリオ名: サード・ジェネレーション
簡易説明: Murderous intent from the green eyes　Green-Eye Curse-Killing
詳細説明 cha 1688: The books of the Niimura main house said that any girl born with green eyes must be killed at once. The Green-Eye Curse-Killing means that when a green-eyed girl has her first period, she gains danger sense and comes to feel an unbearable murderous intent toward others who also have danger sense. A child born green-eyed like this is called 'the third generation,' and her mother is very likely 'the second generation,' that is, someone who, like Natsumi Kogori or Sakura Niimura, has danger sense under certain conditions. Erina Goto surmises that the Green-Eye Curse-Killing is not congenital but is transmitted at birth through contact with the mother's blood. Also, contact with the blood of the first generation, that is, those who used Droga, changes one's constitution into that of the second generation.

簡易説明: Exchange transfusion
詳細説明 cha 1688: Replacing the blood in the body entirely with donor blood by drawing blood from one vessel while transfusing into another at the same time. It is performed to treat severe hemolytic anemia in newborns (anemia that occurs because red blood cells in the body break down faster than new ones can be made), severe liver damage and poisoning in adults, and so on.\n　The exchange transfusion in this story falls under the treatment of 'poisoning': it flushed the Droga components out of Natsumi Kogori's body in an attempt to cure Haruka Niimura's Green-Eye Curse-Killing. As a result, Natsumi Kogori lost her danger sense, but it also seems to have been effective in curing Haruka Niimura.

シナリオ名: パラサイト・プリズン
簡易説明: Honey fungus
詳細説明 cha 1688: A mushroom classified in the order Agaricales, family Tricholomataceae, genus Armillaria, that lives mainly as a parasitic fungus on plants. It is distributed across Eurasia, North America and Africa. This species not only lives by breaking down and absorbing dead plants, but is also strongly parasitic and pathogenic toward living plants. The disease caused by honey fungus parasitism is called "Armillaria root rot," and outbreaks have been reported in fruit trees such as apple, pear, peach, grape and chestnut, in woody plants such as cherry and oak, and in potatoes, carrots and others. The mycelium living in dead plants or in the parasitized parts of living trees does not complete its life cycle in that part alone; it forms strands of mycelium like black tree roots and extends them through the ground, and when they touch dead or living trees some distance away, it sends new mycelium into those as well and parasitizes them.\n　Also, the dark honey fungus (Armillaria ostoyae) in the state of Oregon in the United States is known as the largest living organism in the world, with an estimated weight of 600 tons and an estimated age of 2,400 years. It is not the mushrooms themselves that are large; the mycelial bed spread out underground covers 8.9 square kilometers, a tremendously vast area.

シナリオ名: パラサイト・プリズン
簡易説明: 'Time slip,' the theory of moving through space-time
詳細説明 cha 1688: Whether a time slip is possible has not been proven by current science, but according to Einstein's general theory of relativity, objects with strong gravity warp space-time, and this lends support to time-slip theory. Black holes, wormholes and faster-than-light travel are examples. However, even a tiny object is thought to need an enormous amount of energy to slip through time, let alone something large enough to move a human being, which would be nearly impossible to achieve on Earth. Therefore a time slip cannot be caused on Earth, whether artificially or by accident (though on a cosmic scale, it cannot be called absolutely impossible). Human cold sleep (cold storage) can be cited as a pseudo time slip.

シナリオ名: パラサイト・プリズン
簡易説明: The problem of human teleportation
詳細説明 cha 1688: Teleportation as commonly imagined means moving an object to a distant place without a moment's delay, but physically such a thing is impossible (the time-slip theory described above excepted). There is, however, a way to achieve teleportation in a simulated form: a research team at Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands copies the information of the object to be moved and reproduces it at a position 3 meters away. However, this is the same as creating an object entirely separate from the original, and differs from teleportation as people tend to imagine it. If this were applied to a human, it would be no different from creating a clone at a distant position. In that case, a problem of human bioethics arises. To make it look as if someone had truly teleported, a human clone would have to be created at the distant place and the original human made to vanish. In other words, the original human would be killed. So even if memories and personality could be copied into a human clone, the original would go on existing as before, and to make it truly look like teleportation, serious ethical problems would remain.

シナリオ名: 黙示録のラッパ吹き～開花～
物名: 死月妖花の植物寄生性
簡易説明: Damage to plants by Shigatsu Youka (plant parasitism)
詳細説明 cha 1688: As stated earlier, the honey fungus reproduces vigorously and is strongly parasitic, ravaging the plants around it and making them its seedbed. For this reason it is a mushroom much hated in forestry. Shigatsu Youka is an extreme case of it: its plant parasitism is strong enough to wither the trees and plants around it in an instant, and, as seen in the True Jusatsu Arc, its targets reach beyond plants to mammals, and in the end even to humans. In the cases so far, however, it does not parasitize every living thing; insects and birds suffer no particular harm. Nor do new fruiting bodies sprout from the plants: it merely uses them as a source of nourishment, and its final hosts are mammals, humans included.

シナリオ名: 黙示録のラッパ吹き～伝承～
簡易説明: The oral tradition 'The Sealing of Abaddon,' as told by Erika Niimura
詳細説明 cha 1688: 'The shinigami are the four divine messengers who serve Abaddon. Abaddon appears from a volcano of sulfur. What the Grand Witch must do―is to keep Abaddon and the four divine messengers sealed away.'\n　Erika Niimura was told by the previous Grand Witch to commit this to memory without fail, but it survives nowhere in writing. Erina Goto reasons that the oddly specific substance 'sulfur' points to somewhere connected with a hot spring as the place where Shigatsu Youka is. What is more, the very fact that such lore survives is nothing less than proof that the Arata settlement once lived through a disaster like the present one.

簡易説明: The scientific principle of telepathy
詳細説明 cha 1688:
Telepathy is tele(far)+pathy(feeling): the ability to read the senses of someone far away. It is often classed as paranormal or supernatural science, but in a joint project of the University of Barcelona in Spain, Axilum Robotics, Harvard Medical School, and Starlab, an experiment was run between India and France, 5,000 miles apart. One test subject in India wore a machine that reads the brain's currents and brain waves, and three test subjects in France, wearing separate receiving interfaces, received the signal over the internet. In this very simple test, the sender thought "0" or "1" and the receivers had to sense which; it succeeded. In other words, done the right way, telepathy is not paranormal but an ability that can be produced on purpose. The principle is to detect the faint currents carried to the brain's nerve cells, capture their pattern, and transmit it; in theory, anything the sender perceives through the five senses can be sent and received. However, neurotransmitters, the substances that govern emotion, such as dopamine and adrenaline, cannot be detected by current alone, so it is hard to detect what the sender is thinking or feeling. So it is safest to assume that, for now, telepathy can only exchange the five senses. Abilities that the same principle can explain include
・Thoughtography: capturing the current patterns of the hippocampus, the brain's memory region, and the visual cortex
・Qigong: controlling the blood flow in the practitioner's hands by breathing to deliberately create a weak magnetic field
・Clairvoyance: sensing how much infrared and ultraviolet (both a kind of radio wave) is given off beyond a flimsy barrier
and others.

簡易説明: The exchange diary Kana Niimura wrote entirely out of her own fantasies
詳細説明 cha 1688:
I had planned to write all sorts of things, but it would be far too cruel to Kana Niimura, so I will hold back. My apologies to everyone who was looking forward to it. And please spare me the retort that, after letting those girls die so many times, this is the crueler thing.







































/VAR/-san, do you want to see it that badly?

　A fantasy diary in which Kana Niimura wrote out sickly-sweet daydreams about herself and her classmate Hiroto. Its contents were enough to set her sister, 10 years older, burning with jealousy. At first it kept up some semblance of an exchange diary, but gradually it came to hold nothing but what each likes about the other, what each loves, and their dreams for the future (she probably ran out of material). But she carelessly kept it going every day, even on Sundays and long vacations, so Chigaya Niimura took it for a fake diary and no harm came of it. Had she made it that realistic, another incident besides the curse-killings might well have broken out.
　How Hiroto feels about Kana Niimura is unknown, but he does seem to be a popular boy, and at a school with so few students the competition is presumably all the fiercer. On the routes after Shiyo 800, such as the True Jusatsu Arc, there is no information that Kana Niimura has a boyfriend, so her love probably did not bear fruit.

簡易説明: The scripture of the Arata settlement
詳細説明 cha 1688: Scripture said to record the words of Sele (Ginosuke Niimura), the first Westerner to reach the Arata settlement. It tells less doctrine than what Sele went through before Japan. From the part Chigaya Niimura read:\nThey resembled the cherry, as Japan calls it, but also the rose and the plum. Native to the mother country, it seems, they were called Bonita: 'beautiful' in our tongue. Bonita grew everywhere there and were loved. Then one day, with a great earthquake and the sound of a hideous trumpet, Bonita turned sinister. The giant trees destroyed the towns and covered the sky, and every other tree and flower withered in an instant. Nor was that all. The dead rose and began to slaughter the people. We led armies against them, but could never match an army that could not die. Then, from a volcano of brimstone, there appeared four generals of the army of the dead, called divine messengers, and their demon king―Abaddon. They seemed to command their army with that hideous trumpet; each time it sounded, the dead appeared and towns and nature were destroyed, and it rang so loudly that no one could tell where it came from. The divine messengers had cunning tongues and high intelligence, and one companion after another defected to the dead. Our companions fell prey to suspicion feeding on itself, and at last killed one another. Judging the mother country beyond restoring, I fled by ship to this land. At first I suspected even my companions aboard of being spies for the dead. But join the dead, or sail on with no end in sight―when nothing remained but despair, need I cast aside those who chose the voyage? It was a gamble, but I chose to trust them.

簡易説明: The cell suicide of Shigatsu Youka
詳細説明 cha 1688:
A poison working on its own maker sounds contradictory, but nature has many examples: a venomous snake bitten by its own kind dies, as does a poison dart frog given its own poison. In the human body, too, cells are replaced through the cell suicide called apoptosis, signaled by protein enzymes called caspases (a group of cysteine proteases).
　Shigatsu Youka is the same: a protein enzyme makes its old fungal cells kill themselves. The spores in third-generation blood make far more of it, so contact with that blood sends the self-destruct signal far more strongly than usual (the third-generation spores are altered and do not destroy themselves; strictly, apoptosis is an animal phenomenon, but Shigatsu Youka, a fungus, is an exception).
　Why so much in the third generation? By nature it is likely to be attacked, bleed and die, and the ground around it readily forms fruiting bodies born from the fourth generation. Blood of the dead or dying third generation seeps into that soil and kills the fungal cells at the surface; new cells grow rapidly from below, and the newborn fruiting body joins the mycelial mat more readily (the toxicity fades soon after bleeding, and the blood never touches Shigatsu Youka itself, so harm is slight).
　It has lived by this cycle since ancient times, but human intelligence made it wish for immortality, and it tried to evolve to suppress this cell suicide. Apoptosis itself, basic to its survival, could not be abolished, so it tried to have the divine messengers' bodies undergo, in its place, the cell suicide third-generation blood causes. Hence, once enough third-generation blood clings to them, their bodies rapidly rot and vanish.

簡易説明: The divine messengers, Shigatsu Youka's servants
詳細説明 cha 1688:
The divine messengers exist to give Shigatsu Youka resistance to its weakness, third-generation blood; the four are a living first and second generation and a dead first and second generation. The resistance comes from Shigatsu Youka taking in the spores altered inside their bodies. Once taken in, the divine messengers become one with Shigatsu Youka; mainly their lower bodies are buried in the fruiting body, so they can no longer move from that spot. Their intelligence is badly impaired too, so they can hardly hold a conversation.
　For a living infected person to become a divine messenger, they must will it where Shigatsu Youka's mycelial mat lies. This slows the defenses of the autonomic nervous system, so the hyphae get in easily. The fourth generation, once living infected people, are candidates too, but over time their spores reproduce sexually and change, and they lose their resistance to third-generation blood. Once someone becomes fourth generation, the window for becoming a divine messenger is half a day at most.
　In fact a dead divine messenger differs little from an ordinary corpse; other walking corpses, too, can talk and move with more than human strength, as seen in the story. The only difference is whether there are spores in the body. The same goes for the living: Shigatsu Youka's hyphae quickly enter whoever chooses to become a divine messenger, and they are reborn as one.
　Divine messengers can also turn out incomplete. A first generation who used extremely little Droga has an imperishable body and great physical ability, but at times their former self returns, and then they would be extremely dangerous to Shigatsu Youka.

簡易説明: 能面と赤装束を着ける風習について
詳細説明 cha 1688: 死月妖花によって活動を再開した死体は、その菌糸で作られた縫い目のない白装束をまとう。その白装束は死亡した者の肉体を維持するための、いわゆる神経線維の役割をしており、白装束を脱ぎ捨てるとたちまちのうちに肉体が腐敗し消滅してしまう（短時間であれば脱いで普通の人間に偽装することは可能）。ゆえに荒田の人々は死亡した人間が神使となった場合、それを死神と呼び、さらに死亡した者自体を指すようになった。死亡した第一世代および第二世代が神使になると、生きた第一世代と第二世代を神使になるよう誘惑するので『死神が生者を連れていく』と認識される。\n　それを防ぐために神使と同じ装束を着て死神の目をごまかそうとする風習が出来上がった。さらに第三世代の血は神使および死月妖花に致命傷を与えることができるので、第三世代の血の色を表す赤い装束、翠眼呪殺を防ぐために顔を隠す面を着けるようになった。このように能面と赤装束は神使の目をごまかし、翠眼呪殺を防ぐための格好であり、知恵の結晶と言える。\n　余談ではあるが、能面は普通、額やアゴが見える大きさであり、これは能楽で演者の顔の動きが見えるようにするためである。しかし荒田集落の能面は顔を隠すこと自体を目的としているので、額やアゴまで覆われる大きさになっている。

簡易説明: 不死の生物
詳細説明 cha 1688:
不老不死は人類の永遠の願いと言われることがあるが、生命が地球上に誕生した時には既に不老不死は出来上がっていたと言われている。厳密には事故や病気で死ぬことはあっても自然死――つまり寿命で死ぬことがない。単細胞生物では寿命のないものも多く見られ、多細胞生物ではベニクラゲなどが例に挙げられる。つまり寿命とは、進化の結果得られた機能と言える。
　ではなぜ生物が寿命を備えたかと言えば、種の繁栄が目的と考えられている。単体の生物が死なないということは姿を変えずに生きることと同義で、その短所を挙げるならば環境適応による進化が阻害される点である。単細胞生物のように自身でエネルギーを生成でき（光合成等）、成長速度が早く繁殖力が強ければ、生存環境が著しく変化してもその中の数体が突然変異を起こし適応できる可能性がある。しかし多細胞生物のように繁殖力に乏しくエネルギー生成できない場合、このような環境適応の進化がなくては短期間でその種が全滅する危険性をはらんでいる。またその種が増えすぎると、必要な外部エネルギー（餌）が枯渇することも想像に難くない。
　生物単体で見れば寿命のない方が理想であるが、種全体で見れば次世代の突然変異による進化を期待し、同種内でのエネルギーの取り合いを是正した方がよい。ゆえに死とは子孫のための機能であり、それに逆行することは種の全滅を早めることを意味する。現に地球上で目立って繁栄しているのは、寿命のある多細胞生物の方である。
　不老不死を願うことは、見方によっては生者のエゴに過ぎないとも言えるだろう。

物名: 死月妖花胞子の脳関門突破
簡易説明: 死月妖花の胞子が脳関門を突破する方法
詳細説明 cha 1688: 人間は脳に害となる物質が入り込まないようにするための機構として、血液脳関門(BBB)が存在している。ここで有害物質、大きな物質の浸入阻害、必要な酵素等のやり取りが行われる。通常、胞子ほどの大きさでは侵入することはできないが、死月妖花の胞子は関門直前の血管壁に入り込み、そこで急速に細胞分裂を行い、脳側の血管壁から暴露される。つまり、脳関門を通らず、血管壁内を通過することで脳に到達できるのだ。また、脳室周囲器官(CVO)という脳器官は生命維持のための最重要箇所であるが、脳ホルモン等の分泌物を体内に発散させるため、脳関門なく『脳の窓』と言われている。ここから侵入できるかどうかは不明のままである。
